output:
I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the data.

I wrote `/app/bin/payroll.py` and ran it on `/app/data`, saving the result to `/app/out/payroll.json`. `python3 /app/tools/check_payroll.py` reports every value matching the approved figures. That covers all 150 employees on each field, the four exception counts and the totals.

The script uses only the standard library. It reads all nine site formats and follows the rules in `payroll-rules.md` rather than anything specific to this period's files. I haven't tested it on any other period's data. I also didn't add checks for malformed input beyond what the docs describe.

I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f | head -100; cat docs/*.md

cd /app; sed -n 50,200p docs/exports.md; echo ======; cat docs/output.md | head -60; ls data data/exports data/corrections | head -50; cat data/sites.csv data/period.json; head -5 data/employees.csv data/rates.csv; cat tools/check_payroll.py | head -80

cd /app/data; for s in exports/*; do echo "=== $s $(ls $s | wc -l)"; f=$(ls $s | head -3 | tail -1); head -c 600 $s/$f; echo; done; head -5 corrections/batch-1.csv; file exports/*/* | grep -c gzip; sed -n 80,140p ../tools/check_payroll.py; wc -l employees.csv rates.csv

python3 --version; python3 -c 'import zoneinfo;print(zoneinfo.ZoneInfo("Asia/Kathmandu"))'; cd /app/data; head -c 300 corrections/batch-2.csv; python3 - <<'EOF'
import glob,gzip
n=0
for f in glob.glob('exports/*/*'):
    b=open(f,'rb').read(2)
    if b==b'\x1f\x8b': n+=1; print(f)
print(n)
EOF
cd /app; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/payroll.py data out/payroll.json && python3 tools/check_payroll.py

cd /app; echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Wrote /app/bin/payroll.py implementing the documented formats and rules (stdlib only), ran it on /app/data into /app/out/payroll.json; check_payroll.py reports every value matching."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
